title:
Selecting Microscopic Degrees of Freedom for Emergent Spacetime:
Coupled Quantum Oscillators as the Substrate
content: A lattice of locally coupled quantum oscillators is proposed as a hypothesis for the microscopic substrate from which continuum spacetime and its effective physical contents may ultimately emerge. The elementary coupled oscillator is defined as an elementary substrate unit (ESU): a minimal dynamical and information-bearing quantum degree of freedom, ontologically prior to spacetime, fields, and particles defined within spacetime. Collections of ESUs may form composite substrate structures—including, in principle, chains, loops, sheets, defects, and networks—of which the strings of string theory would represent one possible class rather than the fundamental starting point. The oscillator substrate is evaluated against practical criteria for a viable microscopic architecture, including collective-mode formation, ultraviolet regularization, locality, quantum compatibility, phase structure, tractability, parameter economy, and the capacity to encode and propagate physical information. What the simplest fixed cubic lattice actually demonstrates is more modest than the full hypothesis: its collective-mode dispersion relation yields continuum-like relativistic propagation, with a limiting speed set by microscopic parameters and a calculable Lorentz-violating correction, rather than the emergence of spacetime itself. Taking the lattice spacing at the Planck length, this correction is compared explicitly against current observational bounds on quadratic-order Lorentz violation and found to lie safely within them by roughly eight orders of magnitude for the bosonic sector so far constructed, giving the hypothesis a concrete, numerical falsification target rather than a qualitative one. The fixed lattice is treated as a controlled first stage rather than a complete theory, and explicit failure criteria are identified, including failure to recover a universal low-energy causal structure, a massless spin-2 gravitational sector, dynamical connectivity, and viable chiral matter. The coupled-oscillator substrate is therefore advanced as a concrete and falsifiable hypothesis for the microscopic level from which spacetime, composite structures, fields, particles, and their information-bearing capacities may ultimately arise — and, more distinctively, as a dynamical selection principle whose predictive content lies as much in what its microscopic dynamics forbid as in what they can generate. Only the kinematic first step of this hierarchy—continuum-like collective-mode formation on a fixed lattice—is demonstrated here; the higher levels, including spacetime itself, are stated explicitly as open research problems rather than as established results.
